stories.title: Adani Power Q2 EBITDA rises 60% to Rs 8,231 crore
stories.summary: In its July‑September quarter, Adani Power reported EBITDA of Rs 8,231 crore, a 60 % increase from Rs 5,150 crore in the same quarter a year earlier. The live‑blog noted that the company’s capacity‑expansion programme remains a focus for the period. No net‑profit or revenue figures were provided in the source.
stories.why: The EBITDA jump signals stronger operating performance, a key metric for investors assessing profitability trends.
stories.change: New high-signal event entered the brief.

stories.title: Ohio Democratic Gov. Candidate Amy Acton Calls Opponent’s Attack Ad Despicable
stories.summary: Amy Acton, the Democratic candidate for Ohio governor, described a campaign advertisement from Republican challenger Vivek Ramaswamy as “despicable.” The ad shows Acton’s estranged mother, Donna Arthur, accusing Acton of lying her whole life and omits that Arthur’s husband was charged with raping Acton as a child and that Acton and her brother were later removed from custody. The spot attracted criticism from members of both parties, and President Donald Trump defended it while Ramaswamy posted about it on social media.
stories.why: The controversy illustrates how negative‑campaign tactics can shape voter perceptions in a pivotal statewide race.
stories.previousTitle: Ohio Democratic candidate Amy Acton calls opponent’s ad featuring estranged mother despicable

stories.title: Paris extends curfew as Marseille and Lyon ban protests after riots
stories.summary: Sign In Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Paris is extending a partial curfew restricting movement in parts of the city until Monday, as Marseille and Lyon impose a total ban on protests this weekend. France is still reeling from major disorder at the weekend, when large protests against the high cost of living and school conditions were overshadowed by riots and looting that saw business and historic buildings destroyed.

stories.previousTitle: France extends curfew in Paris and bans protests in Marseille and Lyon amid weekend riots
stories.previousSummary: Paris is extending a partial curfew limiting movement in parts of the city until Monday, while Marseille and Lyon ban all protests this weekend. The Louvre, Orsay and Picasso museums in Paris will also close on Saturday as more demonstrations are expected. France is still dealing with weekend disorder when protests over the cost of living and school conditions were overshadowed by riots and looting that damaged businesses and historic buildings. Only authorised union demonstrations are allowed elsewhere, President Macron said.

stories.title: RBI asks banks, payment firms to forensically clear tech environments in case of a data breach
stories.summary: The RBI has asked financial entities to remove management and administrative interfaces from public internet access, enforce multi-factor authentication for administrative access, and restrict access to cloud and backend systems on a least-privilege basis. The RBI issued the advisory on October 19, shortly after CERT-In warned about the growing use of artificial intelligence agents to carry out cyberattacks.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.
stories.previousTitle: RBI directs banks, payment firms to clear tech environments after data breach
stories.previousSummary: The Reserve Bank of India issued a directive requiring banks and payment service providers to carry out forensic clearance of their technology environments whenever a data breach is reported, to identify and remediate compromised systems and protect customer data. The order is part of the regulator’s effort to reinforce cybersecurity across the financial sector.
